title: Vortex wake of an elastically mounted cylinder
description: Two-dimensional URANS (k-omega SST) re-run in OpenFOAM v2412 of a cylinder free to move across the flow, with the mass ratio, spring stiffness and damping of Martins & Avila (2019, Marine Structures 65); coarser than the published simulations and shown across the span. Render: Q-criterion iso-surfaces and spanwise vorticity, ParaView.
caption: Figure 2. Vortex wake of an elastically mounted cylinder free to move across the flow. Vortex cores are coloured by spanwise vorticity, blue clockwise and red anticlockwise. Coarse two-dimensional re-run with the mass, stiffness and damping of the study, shown across the span; not the published simulations.
credit: Simulation and render: Flavio A. C. Martins

title: 37-member truss before and after sizing
description: The 37-member benchmark of the paper (Fig. 6) sized with a Python re-implementation of the linear indirect method, compared at equal mass with a truss of uniform member areas. Render: tubes with radius proportional to the square root of member area, coloured by axial stress over admissible stress, ParaView.
caption: Figure 3. The 37-member benchmark truss at equal mass, with uniform member areas (top) and after linear sizing (bottom). Tube thickness follows member area; colour is axial stress relative to the admissible stress, with the admissible limits marked on the colour bar.
credit: Computation and render: Flavio A. C. Martins

title: Coherent-structure colouring of Ahmed-body tracks
description: Shake-the-Box particle tracks measured behind the Ahmed body (TU Delft Open Jet Facility), coloured with the Python CSC implementation; the CSC mode is selected against streamwise vorticity from the same measurements. Sparse and dense random subsets of the near-wake tracks, seen along the stream. Render: ParaView.
caption: Figure 4. Coherent-structure colouring of particle tracks measured behind the Ahmed body, seen along the stream, for sparse (left) and dense (right) seeding. Red tracks belong to the trailing vortex; the grey panel is the rear face of the body.
credit: Measurements: TU Delft Aerodynamics Laboratories; analysis and render: Flavio A. C. Martins

title: Wake of an actuator-surface rotor without and with wings
description: Steady RANS runs of the repository's actuator-surface case (rotor only and four wing strips) on the supplied mesh, ported to OpenFOAM v2412. Render: streamwise velocity on cross-flow planes 1, 4, 7 and 10 rotor sizes downstream and streamlines from the actuator ends, ParaView.
caption: Figure 5. Streamwise velocity behind an actuator-surface rotor without wings (left) and with four wing strips (right); dark red is slow wake. With the wings the wake rises and recovers faster. Steady simulations of the repository case.
credit: Simulation and render: Flavio A. C. Martins

title: Lid-driven cavity at Re = 1000
description: Steady lid-driven cavity flow at Re = 1000 computed with the repository's projection solver on a 192 x 192 grid; centreline velocities checked against Ghia, Ghia & Shin (1982). Render: line-integral convolution of the flow direction coloured by vorticity.
caption: Figure 12. Steady lid-driven cavity flow at Re = 1000 from the repository's solver. Texture follows the flow direction; colour is vorticity, blue clockwise and red anticlockwise. Secondary eddies form in both lower corners.
credit: Simulation and render: Flavio A. C. Martins
